During the course of the game, some parts of the map appear covered by a semi-transparent haze, while others are shrouded in complete darkness. This effect is called fog of war.
The dark areas are those that have not yet been explored and about which, naturally, there is no information. When you pass through these areas with your own units, the terrain is revealed and you can see the enemy's units and structures located there.
However, once there are no longer any units or buildings of your own in the explored areas, the haze once again limits your field of view, and although it lets you see the terrain and the structures built there, it prevents you from observing enemy units.

The map of Imperivm III - Great Battles of Rome is a scaled representation of the terrain. You can recognize structures and units by the color of the player they belong to. While seeing enemy buildings on the map only requires passing by them once with one of your units, seeing the units of rival sides requires them to be within the field of view of one of your units or buildings.
To show/hide the map you can use the Space key, the mouse's middle button (if it has one), or the map button located at the bottom of the game screen.
There are two types of resources: food and gold.

Food is produced in villages. Food is essential for maintaining the health of all your units, and it can also be used to increase the population of strongholds (except in the Carthaginian nation) and to recruit units in the Germanic nation.

Gold is collected automatically in strongholds and stored in the Townhall, which is their central structure. You can also store it in outposts, villages, and shipyards. Gold allows you to carry out orders in structures and to recruit units.
Production depends on population. The greater the population of the strongholds, the greater their gold production.

Both food and gold are stored in strongholds, villages, and outposts, and can only be used where they are located. If you want to use gold or food somewhere else, you will have to transport it there with caravans. Naturally, if the caravan is destroyed or captured by the enemy, you will lose all the resources it was carrying.

Capturing structures is an essential element in achieving the final goal of Imperivm III - Great Battles of Rome: military conquest. Mastering this aspect of the game will let you face every mission you take on with every guarantee of success. Each building has a loyalty level that is shown, when the structure is selected, at the top of the screen next to its icon. When it comes under attack, loyalty drops, and if it reaches zero, the building is captured.
In Local Network or Internet games there is a variable number of neutral villages and outposts. These structures are captured immediately by the first player to reach them.

Each soldier can carry up to 20 units of food (the elephant, 50), which it gradually consumes. When its food reserves reach zero, its health decreases. On the minimap, the icon of an empty plate shows you the points on the territory where you have warriors lacking food.
When they feed, units recover health points -quickly if they are inside a structure, and more slowly if they are in an open space-.
If your soldiers are stationed at other points on the map, you need to transport there the food needed to feed them.

Among other virtues, the heroes' leadership ability lets them form groups of up to 50 units willing to obey all their orders. Units assigned to a hero receive part of his experience as a bonus, which is added to each unit's own experience for as long as it remains with the leader. Likewise, some of the hero's special traits affect all the warriors linked to him. To select, move, or give orders to a group, you only need to select, move, or give orders to the hero leading it.
In addition, heroes can order their troops to form up in four different formations, each with the advantages it brings:
Front - Units increase 4 levels while they keep the formation.
Line - Units gain 2 points of attack and defense, and archers' range increases by 20%.
Block - Units gain 6 additional points of defense.
Cavalry core formation - Units gain 4 points of attack, and archers' range increases by 20%.

In addition to the stats common to all units, each hero has 5 special traits that set him apart from the heroes of other nations. The hero and the units linked to him benefit from some of these. From others, only the units benefit. And finally, some special traits only come into play when you activate them. Each unit has a set of stats that set it apart from the rest. On the game screen, some of them appear next to the unit's name and icon.

A unit's health represents its current condition. When the health level reaches zero, the unit dies.
If you select several units, the bar shows the average health of the whole group. If you press the key to the right of L (Ñ on a Spanish keyboard), you can see, above each unit, a green bar representing its health and a blue bar showing its stamina level.

By definition, most warriors have a series of special traits that increase their effectiveness in various ways and that, in addition, make them especially powerful against certain units. Using special traits requires stamina.
To be able to use special traits in combat, the unit must have the minimum stamina value required for it. Otherwise, it will have to wait for its stamina to regenerate until it reaches the required value.

All units have accumulated experience that determines their level. The higher the level, the greater the damage the unit will deal to enemies. Likewise, the less damage it will take from them.
There are several ways to gain experience and, as a result, level up: by assigning units to a hero, through combat, through hunting, through learning, by picking up magic items and amulets, by housing units in military posts, by using orders.
A unit's level appears next to an icon with the letter "N".

The attack value represents the damage a unit deals when it faces an enemy of the same level. That damage depends on its level, on the level and armor value of the attacked unit, on the special traits, and on the stamina of both at the moment of combat.
For example, if a Tribune with "Damage" 40 faces a Gladiator with "Armor" 10, it will inflict 30 points of damage on it. When the "Armor" value is equal to or greater than the damage the enemy could inflict on it, that damage is reduced to 20% of its maximum capacity.

Each unit has a defense value that indicates its degree of protection against its enemies' attacks. In general, it serves to reduce the damage it takes, although whenever it is attacked it will always take at least 20% of its opponent's attack value.
For example, if a Gladiator with "Armor" 10 is attacked by a Tribune with "Damage" 40, it will take 30 points of damage.
Active - The warrior recovers stamina more quickly.
Attack skill - Adds twice the unit's stamina points to its damage value.
Bleeding attack - Inflicts additional damage equal to 10 % of the enemy's maximum health.
Charge - This is a trait of mounted units, which multiplies the unit's attack power by 8 if it has gone more than ten seconds without making an attack.
Combat skill - The warrior regains one point of stamina for every hit inflicted on the enemy.
Cripple - Reduces the target's stamina points to zero.
Curse - Allows the unit to cast a curse on the enemy so that its next attack misses.
Death blow - The unit finishes off the enemy if its health level after taking the damage is below 50%. This special trait has no effect on heroes.
Defense skill - Adds twice the unit's stamina points to its armor value. It is triggered when the unit is hit.
Deflection - Allows the unit to come out unscathed from a blow dealt by an enemy.

Disease attack - The warrior infects its target and makes it sick, constantly draining its health, although it never drops below 10% of its maximum health. The disease's effect disappears when it recovers all its health, for example, by standing next to a well.
Drain - Every successful hit on an opponent reduces the enemy's stamina by 2 points.
Expertise - Eliminates the enemy with a single blow if it is a much weaker opponent. It is not effective against heroes.
Ferocity - The unit regains its maximum stamina level when it defeats an enemy.
Freedom - The warrior cannot be attached to a hero.
Healing - Allied warriors receive 20 more points of health than the level of the unit that has this special trait.
Invisibility - Allows the unit to turn itself or another allied unit invisible.
Keen sight - Reveals all hidden enemies in sight.
Learning - The warrior gains one point of experience for every hit dealt to a more experienced enemy.
Life steal - The unit receives as many points of health as the damage it has dealt to the enemy.
Offensive tactics - Adds the unit's level to its damage value.
Parry - The unit deals no damage, but it also takes none while it has stamina. Every failed attack consumes 1 point of stamina; every hit inflicted grants it 1 point of stamina.
Penetration - Inflicts maximum damage without taking into account the enemy's armor value.
Power strike - If the unit has more than double the health points of the enemy and the enemy takes damage, it will be eliminated. It cannot be used against heroes.

Rage - Increases the attack capacity of the unit that has it at the expense of its own health. The health it loses is converted into additional damage for the enemy. The health loss of the unit that has “Rage” is limited: it can never drop below 50% of its maximum health.
Regeneration - The unit recovers its health more quickly.
Revenge - When the unit is defeated, in revenge it inflicts 100 points of damage on its executioner.
Sneak - The unit is invisible to its enemies if it remains inactive for 10 seconds.
Spike armor - Returns to the attacker all the damage taken in melee combat.
Teaching - The unit that has it grants experience to allied units with less experience than itself.
Toughness - Gains 5 points of maximum health.
Trample - The unit that has it deals damage to all enemies around it on the battlefield.
Triple strike - The warrior triples his damage.
Triumph - The warrior gets healed upon killing an enemy.

In the “Great Battles” game mode, as you progress, you will meet characters who will tell you about the objectives you must achieve. Some of these objectives are vital to the development of the story. Others are optional, but they will give you bonuses of enormous use in successfully completing your mission: a level increase, magic items, amulets, additional troops... Each time you receive a new mission, a message appears in the message window. Likewise, when the mission's objective is achieved, the message disappears.

Choose how you want to receive help during the game: Automatic - When relevant, the program displays a window with valuable information to help you progress in the game. Manual - A text appears in the lower left corner of the screen to let you know a help message has arrived. Click the text to view its content. You can turn off help by selecting the “Off” option.

They are the inhabitants of villages and strongholds. The larger the population of a village or stronghold, the more resources it produces. Groups of peasants can be summoned to move them to another village or stronghold.

Caravans (camels, mules and carts) can carry up to 1,000 units of gold or food. They are used to move resources between settlements and to supply units with food. Caravans can be attacked and captured by the enemy. If this happens, you will lose all the resources they are carrying.
The boat is a supply unit capable of transporting resources between shipyards and supplying food to units.
Ships are equipped to attack other ships or land targets. They can carry a maximum of 60 warriors.

The catapult is a wooden device built by warriors to launch projectiles at a chosen target. 10 is the maximum number of units you can assign to building the catapult. The more warriors you use for this task, the faster the construction will be. Due to its poor accuracy, the catapult is more effective when used to attack buildings.
A ram is a siege device designed to destroy the gates of an enemy stronghold. You can assign a maximum of 10 units to its construction. The ram will automatically head for the nearest gate.

Ghouls are creatures from the afterlife that are temporarily summoned to our world. Although they do not attack directly, they are able to drain the life of the units that pass close to them. Once their time expires, they return to the world of the dead.

Walls defend the interior of strongholds. Sentries patrol to warn of any threat. Gates close automatically when the enemy's presence is detected. Towers fire upon the enemy. The greater the stronghold's population, the higher the rate of fire from the towers.

Teuton Tents are isolated settlements where Germanic mercenary warriors take refuge. A neutral camp can shelter up to 40 cavalry and archers. If you manage to defeat its garrison, 12 of the units housed in the Teuton Tent will join your army. In addition, for every 400 units of food you bring to the camp, a new Teuton will enter your service.

Sacrificial altars are sacred places where druids, priests, shamans, priestesses or enchantresses perform powerful rituals that affect all units, both allied and enemy. Each ritual requires a certain mystical energy, which is obtained when spiritual units gather at the altar. The more druids, priests, shamans, priestesses or enchantresses take part, the faster the regeneration.
Built by the shamans in honor of the god Moloch, sacred sacrifices are performed in these places.
Wind of wisdom Increases by 1 the level of all existing units (friendly and enemy) with a level below 20. (Recharge points: 10).
Starvation For two minutes, reduces the food of every stronghold, outpost, village and caravan, whether friendly or enemy. (Recharge points: 20). Requires 20 charges.
Soothing rain Every 5 seconds restores 1 point of stamina to all nearby units. Its effect lasts 30 seconds. (Recharge points: 30).
Last Sacrifice For one minute, decreases the health of all friendly and enemy units. (Recharge points: 50).
Bloodlust For one minute, all allied warriors can attack without regard for the enemy's defense value. (Recharge points: 60).

Remnants of other times, ruins often hold treasures. But don't get too confident... they say ruins are also full of dangers. Only heroes of a certain level dare to enter and manage to return with a valuable item. At the top of the screen, when the ruins are selected, you can see the item hidden within them and the level required to obtain it.

Teleports are underground passages that connect two distant locations. Units and armies use them to move quickly from one place to another without being detected, allowing them to take the enemy by surprise.

Wells are places blessed by the druids and endowed with healing power. A wounded unit need only approach a well to begin recovering its health. From wells it is also sometimes possible to draw a little healing water to carry to other places.

Each hero, warrior or spirit character can carry up to 4 magic items or amulets. Some items must be used to take effect, while others take effect simply by being carried by the warriors. A third group has both characteristics. To use them, just double-click the item's icon.
Amulet of Triumph Returns 100 points of health to its bearer when it defeats an enemy.
Armor charm Until it defeats its first opponent, the warrior will have 4 additional points of defense.
Bear teeth amulet Increases its bearer's maximum attack capacity by 4 points.
Belt of might Increases its bearer's defense capacity by 4 points.
Concentration stone Increases its bearer's maximum attack capacity by 60 points. When used, it heals its bearer by taking stamina from an allied unit.
Damage charm The warrior enjoys 4 additional points of attack. The effect disappears when it defeats its first enemy.
Gem of Wisdom If a warrior linked to a hero is defeated, there is a 50% chance that the hero will receive part of its experience.
God's Gift The bearer of this item fully recovers its health when it eliminates an enemy unit. The item then disappears.
Golden Ankh Gives its bearer 500 points of health and 8 of attack.
Healing herbs Restore health to their bearer.
Healing water Distributes up to 2,000 points of health among nearby allied units.
Health charm Increases by 40 the health points of the unit that carries it, until it manages to eliminate an enemy unit.
Herb amulet of luck Adds 20 points of defense to its bearer.
Knowledge charm This charm adds 4 levels to warriors. The effect disappears when it manages to defeat an enemy unit.
Noble Defense Warriors with a level higher than 12 will gain 4 additional points of defense when they defeat their first enemy.
Noble Offense Warriors with a level higher than 12 will gain 4 additional points of attack when they defeat their first enemy.
Ring of Power Increases its bearer's damage value by 20 points. Also, once recharged, it heals the warrior carrying it.
Scroll of Death All warriors linked to a hero who fall in combat have a 10% chance of turning into vampire spirits.

Veteran Defense Increases its bearer's armor value by 20%.
